BLOCKER: AC-4 quota enforcement is not designed: `go/edpsvc/internal/limits/quota.go` is cited as evidence/control target but is absent from affected_files/review_scope, with no quota config, enforcement point, persistence/consistency model, or per-store behavioral test.

AC-2 control mapping is wrong: runtime entrypoint is Go `cmd/explain`/`explain.Capture`, but CTL-EXPLAIN-SAMPLING and AC-2 evidence/check target `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`; sampling cap, allowlist, rollback, and redaction are not tied to the actual runtime path.
MAJOR: SLO rules/dashboard are delivered in Slice 1 while measured baselines arrive in Slice 4, contradicting the invariant that thresholds come from measured baselines; no baseline-to-config linkage or validation prevents aspirational SLOs.
Generated Prometheus rules and Grafana dashboard lack `promtool`/Grafana schema validation and drift checks in the test matrix, so the single-source config invariant is not enforced.
Degradation auto-expiry persistence and renewal limits are undefined; file-based config may not expire without reload, and repeated renewals can mask failures despite `max_duration<=15m`.
EXPLAIN sampling is probability-capped only; no global/per-query rate limit or load-shed budget means 0.05 sampling can still overload production at high QPS.

Benchmark repeatability protocol is underspecified: no warmup, iteration count, outlier policy, or deterministic dataset provisioning; “six store groups” is also not mapped to the AC’s DB/object/cache/queue stores.
AC-1 recorded baselines have no defined artifact schema/path per store; only `engineering/benchmarks/BI-PF-1314/README.md` is listed, so baseline evidence cannot be reviewed.
MINOR: `run_timestamp` is listed among benchmark metrics; if emitted as a label it violates the bounded-cardinality/no-high-cardinality-label invariant.
`failure_taxonomy` omits `BENCH_STORE_SKIPPED` and `CONFIG_INVALID`, which appear in the failure matrix.
Scope/component lists omit `go/edpsvc/internal/explain` and `cmd/explain` despite being declared files and AC-2 entrypoints.
EXPLAIN artifact retention, access-control, and redaction details are asserted but not concretely specified or tested.
Synthetic `t-bench` tenant provisioning/cleanup is not defined, so RLS-scoped non-empty-read assertions may be non-deterministic.
NIT: Only `docs/EDP-22-BENCHMARKS-SLOS.md` is listed as evidence; no operator runbook link for enabling sampling/degradation is declared.
`runtime_capability: false` on AC-2/AC-3/AC-4 coverage is unexplained and conflicts with “tooling available/demonstrated” acceptance language.
SUMMARY: Design direction is sound, but Gate-1 readiness is blocked by quota-enforcement and EXPLAIN control gaps.
Top risks: SLO thresholds not grounded in measured baselines, generated artifacts not validated, and degradation expiry/renewal semantics undefined.
Baseline artifact definition and per-store behavioral evidence need to be explicit before approval.
